      • getAccessDenialMessage

        @Nullable
public java.lang.String getAccessDenialMessage(@Nonnull
                                                         org.bukkit.block.Block b,
                                                         @Nonnull
                                                         org.bukkit.entity.Player p)
        Why canOpen(org.bukkit.block.Block, org.bukkit.entity.Player) refused, as a message shown to p instead of the generic "not permitted to access this block".
        Parameters:
        b - The block being opened
        p - The player opening it
        Returns:
        The message to show, or null for the generic permission one
        Implementation Note:
        Override when a preset refuses for a reason the player can act on - a bespoke multiblock that is not finished, say. The default is null, meaning the refusal really is a permission one and the generic message is right.

      • setHeaderItemSlot

        public final void setHeaderItemSlot(int slot)
        Declares slot as this preset's header item: the decorative slot whose colour becomes this menu's GUI title colour. Call from init(), after that slot's item has been added - a preset should declare one whenever it has such a slot, rather than relying on the (implicit) name-matching heuristic that runs when neither this nor optOutOfHeaderItem(ChatColor) was called.
        Parameters:
        slot - The slot holding this preset's header item

      • optOutOfHeaderItem

        public final void optOutOfHeaderItem(@Nonnull
                                     org.bukkit.ChatColor color)
        Explicitly declares that a header item makes no sense for this preset, and that its GUI title should use color instead. Call from init(). This takes precedence over the name-matching heuristic, so a background slot that happens to repeat the item's own name can never override a deliberate opt-out.
        Parameters:
        color - The title colour to use in place of a header item

      • optOutOfHeaderItem

        public final void optOutOfHeaderItem()
        Explicitly declares that a header item makes no sense for this preset, and that its GUI title should take the colour of this machine's own item name instead. Call from init(). This is the declaration to use when a menu has no decorative slot repeating the machine's name, which is almost all of them - it keeps the title colour in items.yml rather than duplicating a ChatColor literal at every call site.
